data.name: Hunger Dungeon
data.detailed_description:
🔔OUR NEW PROJECT "LAST COMMAND"🔔


OUR NEW PROJECT "LAST COMMAND"


Hi every one. I'm Back. And I develop the new game Last Command.
The game is a new action game that combines the elements of the classic game Snake game and the barrage.
If you like Hunger Dungeon. I think you will be like it too!
Plz share or add wishlist this game. This time I need your help.


Acerca do jogo



"Hunger Dungeon" is a 1-6 player round-based Multiplayer Online Battle Arena game.
Enter a cutthroat arena with more than 12 heroes including the Dwarf Forgemaster, Octo Pirate, Princess Ranger, and the Demonic Knight!

  • Compete in absolute chaos in Free-for-All or group up and take on other players in classic Team Deathmatch.
  • Mix and match Spell Scrolls and equipment between rounds to optimize your build (like a MOBA).
  • Utilize positive and negative status effects to your advantage!
  • Or...for those wishing for a greater challenge. Recruit up to 3 other players to take on Dragon Mode, facing off against one of three powerful element dragons for exclusive rewards!


Goblin Profiteer

  1. Collecting Gold increases damage dealt
  2. Collides with opponents head-on

Octo Pirate

  1. Leaves a trail of poisonous Dirty Water
  2. Fires a Death Cannon

Princess Ranger

  1. Conceals in the terrain
  2. Sets traps to immobilize enemies

Element Fuse

  1. Temporarily reduces cooldown of Spell Scrolls
  2. Increased Mana regeneration


  • 2D top-down battle style - with a pixel-art aesthetic
  • Free-to-play - four free players available each week, in-game currency to earn permanent Hero unlocks
  • Up to 6 player online matches - Free-for-All and Team Deathmatch
  • A roster of distinctive characters - each with unique skills and effects
  • 30+ Spell Scrolls - fireballs, lightning bolts, and ice bombs devastate your opponents
  • 40+ items to equip - turn the tide with unique magical equipment with various effects
  • 40+ stages to explore - battle in lush forests, painful volcanoes, or frozen tundras

reviews.review:
Hunger Dungeon is an entertaining free-to-play multiplayer arena game that blends fast-paced combat with strategic character customization and charming pixel-art visuals. Developed and published by No Stuck Game Studio, the game offers a refreshing alternative to traditional multiplayer online battle arenas by focusing on shorter encounters, distinctive heroes, and flexible combat strategies. Rather than overwhelming players with complicated objectives or lengthy matches, it emphasizes quick reactions, tactical decision-making, and experimentation with different abilities. Its accessible concept makes it appealing to casual competitors, while its extensive customization systems provide additional depth for players willing to master its mechanics.

The central gameplay revolves around competitive battles accommodating up to six players, with Free-for-All and Team Deathmatch modes offering different approaches to combat. Free-for-All encourages individual survival, careful positioning, and opportunistic attacks, while Team Deathmatch rewards cooperation and effective coordination between teammates. The relatively small player count keeps encounters focused and intense, allowing individual decisions to have a noticeable impact on the outcome. However, the multiplayer-focused structure also means that enjoyment can depend on finding active opponents and reasonably balanced matches.

One of the game's greatest strengths is its diverse roster of playable characters, each possessing distinctive abilities and combat characteristics. Heroes such as the Goblin Profiteer, Octo Pirate, Princess Ranger, and Element Fuse demonstrate the variety of available playstyles. Some characters specialize in direct aggression, while others rely on traps, magical attacks, resource accumulation, or tactical positioning. This diversity encourages experimentation and gives players opportunities to develop strategies that complement their preferences. Learning the strengths and weaknesses of different heroes becomes an essential part of improving performance.

Character customization adds another layer of complexity through more than thirty Spell Scrolls and over forty equipment options. Players can incorporate magical attacks, defensive enhancements, and specialized effects into their builds, creating combinations suited to particular opponents or situations. The ability to adjust equipment between rounds makes encounters more dynamic because players can respond to unsuccessful strategies rather than remaining committed to a single approach. Status effects further enrich combat by introducing temporary advantages and disadvantages that influence movement, offensive capabilities, and survivability. Although these mechanics create substantial strategic possibilities, newcomers may initially struggle to understand the numerous combinations.

Environmental variety contributes significantly to the game's presentation. With more than forty stages featuring forests, volcanic regions, frozen landscapes, and other fantasy locations, Hunger Dungeon provides a colorful collection of battlegrounds. Its top-down pixel-art perspective complements the action by making characters and nearby threats relatively easy to identify. The retro-inspired visuals give the game personality without demanding powerful hardware. Nevertheless, battles involving numerous projectiles, magical effects, and overlapping abilities can become visually chaotic, occasionally making it difficult to follow every interaction.

Beyond competitive multiplayer, Dragon Mode introduces cooperative battles against powerful elemental dragons. Supporting up to four participants, this mode shifts the emphasis toward teamwork, coordinated attacks, and overcoming formidable enemies. The availability of three dragon encounters and exclusive rewards provides additional motivation to explore this alternative experience. Although its limited selection of bosses may eventually become repetitive, Dragon Mode is a worthwhile addition that broadens the game's appeal beyond conventional player-versus-player competition.

The free-to-play progression system offers another attractive feature. Four heroes are available through a rotating weekly selection, allowing players to experiment with different characters before permanently unlocking their favorites using in-game currency. This approach creates meaningful progression goals without requiring an immediate purchase. However, rotating availability may frustrate players who cannot consistently access their preferred characters. The presence of optional purchases also makes progression balance an important consideration, particularly for those who prefer unrestricted character selection.

Despite its promising mechanics, Hunger Dungeon has limitations that prevent it from reaching its full potential. Its dependence on multiplayer participation can create difficulties when matchmaking activity is limited, while the large selection of abilities and equipment introduces potential balancing concerns. New players may encounter experienced opponents with considerably greater knowledge of effective builds, making early matches challenging. Furthermore, its relatively straightforward presentation and repetitive arena structure may not satisfy players seeking elaborate campaigns, extensive storytelling, or substantial single-player content.

Hunger Dungeon also benefits from modest hardware requirements and broad language support, making it approachable for players using less powerful computers. Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, the game has no confirmed official Verified or Playable classification on its Steam listing. Although it supports SteamOS and Linux and has relatively lightweight technical requirements, proper controller functionality, interface readability, and online performance on the handheld remain unverified. Players should therefore consider Steam Deck compatibility unconfirmed rather than assume the game will operate flawlessly.

Overall, Hunger Dungeon is an imaginative multiplayer experience that combines accessible arena battles with surprisingly extensive customization. Its colorful presentation, distinctive heroes, tactical equipment, and cooperative Dragon Mode create a compelling foundation for repeated play. While matchmaking uncertainty, potential balance issues, and a learning curve may discourage some players, its free-to-play accessibility makes it worth exploring for fans of competitive action games. It is particularly appealing to those who enjoy experimenting with different builds and competing alongside friends.

A creative and enjoyable pixel-art arena battler with engaging character variety and meaningful tactical depth, held back by its dependence on multiplayer activity, possible balancing concerns, and unconfirmed Steam Deck compatibility.

Rating: 7/10
